# Closure and Escalation Notes

**Object ID Enumeration - One Client Walking Single-Owner Objects** · `T1190_object_id_enumeration` · [T1190](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1190_object_id_enumeration for <c-ip> at <window start, UTC>
Observed:     <n> distinct cs-uri-stem from c-ip <value> in the 1m window: <values>
Checked:      1. List the object IDs requested and the status of each response -> <result>
              2. Check whether the authenticated user owns any of them (application records) -> <result>
              3. Resolve the client address and the account used -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | support_console (proposed)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- Support or administration consoles that open several users' records in a minute
- Load tests that request many objects by ID

Never tune:
- Never remove the denied walks (401 / 403) from the count - a denied walk is the attacker learning where the check holds.
- Never raise the threshold without re-reading the guarantee: 2T-1 distinct objects is the smallest walk that always alerts (5 for T=3).

## Escalation to incident response

```text

Who / where:  <account> on <host>; source <host or address, if any>
Risk:         base 55 + <conditions met> = <score>
Preserved:    Access-log lines for the client and window -> <where it is saved>
              Application records of object ownership for the IDs requested -> <where it is saved>
              Authentication records of the account used -> <where it is saved>
Containment:  none yet | <action taken, time UTC>
Recommended:  Block the client, suspend the account used, fix the authorization check, and assess the exposed records for notification duties
```

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. Objects the user does not own were served with 200
2. The walk continued past a few IDs or came back in later windows
3. The same client also triggered the API-probing correlation

Risk conditions: host is critical +15 · outside business hours +10 · approved change window -30.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Block or rate-limit the client address
2. Suspend the account used for the walk
3. Disable the vulnerable endpoint until the ownership check is fixed
